title: slim prober: prefill sampler + quant soft-guard
author: Arjun Menon
release_notes: Adds a lightweight prefill prober sidecar to collect compact workload signals and a conservative quantization soft-guard that enables safe rollbacks during canary. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: We frequently need a low-cost sampling path to discover tenant prefill shapes and cold-start ratios for better default batching/caching and quantization recommendations. Larger profilers add cost and complexity during onboarding. This PR introduces a slimline prefill prober (sidecar) plus a conservative 'soft-guard' layer for quant profile rollouts to reduce unit-econ regressions while allowing aggressive trialing in canaries.

Summary of changes: single continuous description with commits, file-level summary, tests and review threads.

What this does: adds a minimal sidecar that samples a configurable percentage of incoming requests' token-length distribution and prefix reuse heuristics; emits compact telemetry and local sketches (count-min + histograms) for the optimizer. Adds a quant soft-guard that: 1) evaluates candidate quant profiles server-side in a low-fidelity simulator, 2) assigns a risk score, and 3) blocks automatic tenant-wide promotion if risk > threshold (with a telemetry-driven override). Also wires a canary flow to allow restricted rollout and an automatic safe-rollback when quality regressions are detected.

Design notes: the prober intentionally avoids full KV cache capture to reduce storage and privacy scope; all sketches are kept per-tenant and TTL'd. Metrics are labeled for model, tenant, route, and observed sequence-length bucket. The soft-guard uses sampled outputs + a lightweight quality fingerprint (BLEU-like delta for deterministic evals, token-entropy delta for generative paths) to detect regressions.

Commits: - b1f4c2a: add slim prober sidecar and config knobs - a9d44f7: telemetry schema and compact histogram encoder - 0c3be11: quant soft-guard runtime check + risk calculator - 7f2d992: canary/rollback controller and CLI flags - 2a8b5ef: TS SDK hooks and small example for console - e1f0c3d: unit/integration tests and benchmarks

Files changed (high-level): - pkg/prefill/prober.go: sidecar worker, sampling logic, sketch encoder - runtime/quant/softguard.go: risk scoring and rollout gating - telemetry/schemas/prefill_metrics.yaml: compact metric shapes - console/examples/prefill-demo.md: usage and config snippets - sdk/typescript/hooks/prefill.ts: hook to expose sampled stats to the Console - tools/canary-controller/canary.go: lightweight canary controller and rollback path - tests/prefill/prober_test.go, tests/quant/softguard_test.go - charts/prefill-sidecar/values.yaml: helm defaults for Private/Dedicated installs

Small code excerpt (illustrative): "func SampleAndSketch(req Request) { if rand.Float32() > cfg.SampleRate { return } sketch.Add(req.Tokens.Len()) emitCompactMetric(sketch.Flush()) }"

Benchmarks & results (local microbench): - prefiller CPU overhead: ~0.6% at 1% sample rate - telemetry payload: ~1.3KB per minute per 10k reqs (compressed) - quant soft-guard simulation: 8-15ms per candidate profile on a 4-vCPU test harness - end-to-end unit-econ impact in tests: median per-token CPU down 3.2% after safe rollouts, max observed quality delta within configured thresholds.

Testing: unit tests for sampling/sketch correctness, integration tests for soft-guard gating, end-to-end simulation with synthetic workloads. Added smoke test to CI that runs a tiny canary flow (30s).

Review conversation (highlights): 
- Maya Chen (reviewer): "Can we guarantee prober telemetry doesn't include any user PII?"
  - Arjun: "Yes — prober only records token-lengths, prefix-hash (one-way salted), and sequence buckets. No text copied. Added unit tests to validate no raw_text fields are emitted."
- Liam O'Connor: "Risk scoring looks good; can we expose the threshold as a tenant opt-in?"
  - Arjun: "Added tenant-level override in the helm values and Console toggle; default remains platform-controlled."
- Sofia Alvarez: "Concerned about the extra 15ms simulation time for large candidate sets."
  - Arjun: "We limit simulations to the top-3 candidate profiles in canary; added an adaptive timeout and a circuit-breaker if simulation exceeds 50ms per-request flow."

CI: All checks passed after two reruns. One flaky unit test (quant_sim_test) was flapping; fixed by replacing a time-dependent seed with deterministic fixture. CI summary: build (pass), unit (pass), integration (pass), e2e-smoke (pass), lint (pass).

Backward compatibility & upgrade notes: this is additive; sidecar can be deployed independently. Helm chart defaults keep the prober disabled for air-gapped installs by default. No breaking API changes.

Merging: Squash merge after signoff. Merged by Maya Chen on 2024-11-20; merge method: squash.

Follow-ups / TODOs: - Add an opt-in dashboard in Console for prefill heatmaps (ENG-3187) - Export compact sketches to the unit-econ simulator for long-run profiling - Add privacy review ticket for EU deployments (PM-513).
additional_context: Canary flow tested against staging tenant 'acme-corp'
